questions.question: Distinguish thermoplastics from thermosets in terms of structure, behaviour on heating, recycling and examples.
questions.expected_answer: Thermoplastics have long polymer chains lying beside one another, held only by weak forces, so heat lets the chains slide: the plastic softens, melts and can be moulded, then sets on cooling, and this can be repeated, which makes them recyclable by remelting; examples are polyethylene, polypropylene, PET, PVC, polystyrene and nylon, all the plastics with recycling codes. Thermosets have chains chemically cross-linked into a three-dimensional network during manufacture, so heating cannot make them flow; they stay rigid until they char and decompose, cannot be remelted or recycled by melting, and are used where heat resistance, rigidity and insulation matter; examples are Bakelite plugs and pot handles, melamine trays and worktops, epoxy and polyester resin.

questions.question: List the main properties of plastics and three weaknesses, giving a use that depends on each property.
questions.expected_answer: Plastics are low in density, so buckets, pipes and car parts are light; strong for their mass and stiffened by thickness, ribs or glass fibre; tough, as in polypropylene crates that survive knocks; flexible, as in bags, hoses and living hinges; electrical insulators, used for cable sheathing, plugs and tool handles; poor heat conductors, used for kettle handles and polystyrene cool-boxes; resistant to water and many chemicals, so PVC pipes and HDPE drums do not rust or rot; and easily moulded into complex, coloured, clear or opaque shapes. Weaknesses: they soften at low temperatures, roughly 80 to 200 degrees; ultraviolet light makes them brittle and chalky outdoors unless stabilised; and many burn, sometimes with toxic smoke, while their resistance to decay makes discarded plastic a lasting pollutant.

questions.question: Explain, with reasons, the choice of plastic for a cooldrink bottle, a bread bag, an outdoor chair and an electrical plug.
questions.expected_answer: A cooldrink bottle is PET because it is clear, light, strong enough to hold the pressure of a fizzy drink, slow to let gas escape and easy to recycle. A bread bag is LDPE because it is flexible, cheap and keeps moisture in. An outdoor chair is polypropylene with a UV stabiliser because it is tough, light and cheap to mould, and the stabiliser stops sunlight making it brittle, which is why unstabilised cheap chairs crack. An electrical plug is a thermoset such as Bakelite or urea-formaldehyde because it must remain rigid and electrically insulating even if the cable overheats, charring rather than melting and dripping.
